messages:
Maya: Heads-up — competitor just announced an "adaptive-routing" offering that routes to cheaper model variants based on cost/latency; ACME pilot asked if we can match their cost/latency. Need quick call: parity vs differentiator.
Chris: Oof. parity requires routing + model-variant compatibility, quantization profiles, and cache handling. Not trivial.
Samir: Let's scope options: parity = 1) routing policy, 2) cheap model variants + quantized runner, 3) prefix/KV guardrails. Differentiator = advanced routing + per-tenant cost controls + UX.
Alejandra: Design risk: parity risks visible quality regressions; we'll need clear labeling and fallback flows :warning:
Eli: Sales note: 3 enterprise pilots pushed this last quarter. If we punt we risk churn. Target from customers: cost/req < $0.01 for batch workloads.
Maya: Proposed plan: 2-week spike to validate parity feasibility -> prototype routing + perf numbers -> decision. Decision criteria: <=70ms added latency, <=10% quality regression on eval set, cost delta <=20%.
Chris: Rough effort estimate: spike = 2 devs x 2wks, prototype routing layer + quantized model runner. Quick bench command: `tools/bench/routing_smoke.py --batch 8 --variant=q4_0`.
Samir: Lower-effort alternative: "compat shim" that routes to cheap model only for non-critical routes (best-effort). Keeps prod quality baseline, fewer infra changes.
Alejandra: If shim, add explicit UI state: "Cost-optimized response — may be less precise" and a toggle in Console. Also telemetry to show before/after quality.
Maya: Decision ask: approve spike (validate architecture) or go straight to shim (faster, less risk)? I'd prefer spike to avoid repeated rework. @Chris can you post ETA + risk note by EOD?
Chris: Yep. I'll draft an RFC with perf estimates, infra risks (KV cache invalidation, autoscale burst exposure), and a roll-forward plan by 17:00 PST.
deploy-bot: Benchmark infra provisioning scheduled: perf cluster will be available 18:00 UTC for spike tests :rocket:
Eli: I'll align ACME pilot PM and collect representative query samples to feed the spike eval.
Maya: Action items recap: Chris RFC by EOD, Eli coordinate pilot samples, Samir own spike backlog, Alejandra draft label copy + telemetry requirements. Back here tomorrow for a go/no-go. :thumbsup:
